## Probe result — the issue-creation path mangles it as well, so the scope is wider than the card's opening line

The body above was composed locally, written once through `POST /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues`, and read back from the API response. Counting by the character immediately following each `(?!`:

| character after `(?!` | local file | stored issue body |
|---|---:|---:|
| an opening square bracket | **1** | **0** |
| a backtick | 6 | 6 |
| a backslash | 3 | 3 |

⇒ the single lookahead-plus-character-class was mangled; **all nine** survivors in the same body came through intact. One probe, nine same-body controls, one write.

### What the scope is now

- **Confirmed mangling:** `POST /issues/{n}/comments` (objectui, 4 of 4) and `POST /issues` (objectstack, 1 of 1). Different repositories, different endpoints, same substitution.
- **Confirmed surviving spellings**, in both writes: `(?!\w)` and a bang followed by a backtick. `(?!\w)` is the workaround to publish.
- ⛔ **Still not covered and still not claimed:** the MCP write path, `PATCH` of a PR or issue body, and whether the trigger is a character class specifically or a wider set of following characters. Two endpoints agreeing is not the same as the whole write surface, and one following character tested against two survivor shapes is not a characterisation.

⇒ the sentence in the card body reading *"Not covered: … issue creation"* is now **out of date by one line**, which is what the probe was for. ⛔ I am not editing the body to hide that — the card says to read this comment first, and the superseded line is the evidence that the probe was worth riding along.

⚠️ The sequence printed in the card's own "probe" sentence is therefore **mangled as stored**, exactly as predicted there. That mangled text is the specimen; ⛔ do not copy it into a command.

### The cheap method, since it is the transferable part

Put the literal in a write you already owe, read the response body back, and compare **by first differing index**, never by length or by eye. Two bodies always differ in length for innocent reasons — a server-appended footer here — and a two-byte substitution inside a regex is invisible in rendered Markdown. Cost of this reading: one probe line in a card that was being filed anyway.
